cues.zh: 我记得小时候，为了等我最喜欢的电视节目开播，要等上一个小时，
cues.en: I remember when I was a kid waiting an hour for my favorite TV show to come on,

cues.zh: 那个节目叫Sharon, Lois & Bram。
cues.en: which was Sharon, Lois & Bram.

cues.zh: 那感觉像是永恒，但随着年龄增长，一切似乎都加快了。
cues.en: That felt like eternity, but as I've gotten older, everything seems to have sped up.

cues.zh: 时间过得快多了。这几乎是所有人都认同的。
cues.en: Time is going much faster. That's something virtually everyone agrees upon.

cues.zh: “是啊，我感觉——我感觉确实是这样。”
cues.en: "Yeah, I feel like- I feel like it does."

cues.zh: “天哪，快太多了。”
cues.en: "Oh man, so much."

cues.zh: “每一年都好像越来越快。”
cues.en: "Each year sort of gets faster and faster."

cues.zh: 但为什么会这样呢？这仅仅是错觉，还是有确凿的科学理由解释为什么时间似乎会随着我们变老
cues.en: But why is this? Is it just an illusion or are there good scientific reasons why time appears to go faster

cues.zh: 而加快呢？
cues.en: as we get older?

cues.zh: 嗯，我正在与国家地理频道的《大脑游戏》合作，这个节目通过实验和互动游戏来探索
cues.en: Well, I'm working with the National Geographic Channel's Brain Games, a show that explores

cues.zh: 人类心智的内部运作，以验证一些
cues.en: the inner workings of the human mind through experiments and interactive games to test out some

cues.zh: 关于这种现象为何发生的理论。
cues.en: theories about why this actually occurs.

cues.zh: 有个听起来挺有道理的说法：每一年过得越来越快，是因为它在
cues.en: There is a reasonable sounding argument that says each year goes faster because it makes up a smaller fraction

cues.zh: 你整个生命中所占的比例越来越小。
cues.en: of your entire life.

cues.zh: “假设我才20岁，一年只是我年龄的1/20。但当我67岁时，一年就是我年龄的1/67。”
cues.en: "Let's say I was only 20. One year is only 1/20th of my age. But when I'm 67, one year is 1/67th of my age."

cues.zh: 这张图显示了在每个年龄，一年占你生命的百分比。
cues.en: This graph shows one year as a percentage of your life at each age.

cues.zh: 但我觉得奇怪的是，如果你把曲线下方的面积加起来，你会发现你到6岁时
cues.en: But what I find weird about this is if you add up the area underneath the curve, you'll find that you've already

cues.zh: 就已经度过了总量的一半。
cues.en: lived half of the total by age 6.

cues.zh: 所以，我真不觉得我们的大脑是这样感知时间的。
cues.en: So, I really don't think this is how our brains perceive time.

cues.zh: 你真觉得，现在的一天就像——
cues.en: You really think that, like, a day now is-

cues.zh: “当然不是。”【笑声】
cues.en: "Of course not." [laughter]

cues.zh: 我认为有更好的理由解释为什么随着年龄增长，时间似乎会加速。
cues.en: I think there are better reasons why time appears to speed up as we get older.

cues.zh: 所以我来到威尼斯海滩，寻找两群人：年长者和年轻者，
cues.en: So I've come to Venice Beach to find two groups of people: The older and younger

cues.zh: 看看他们对时间的感知是否不同。
cues.en: to see if their perceptions of time differ.

cues.zh: 我想做的是启动计时器，然后不看时间，
cues.en: So what I want to do is I want to set my timer going and without counting,

cues.zh: 你觉得一分钟到了就告诉我。
cues.en: you tell me when you think a minute is up.

cues.zh: “开始吧。”
cues.en: "Let's go."

cues.zh: 开始。
cues.en: Start.

cues.zh: “好的。”
cues.en: "Okay."

cues.zh: 世界各地做这个实验时，老年人通常会高估时间，
cues.en: Everywhere around the world, when this experiment is performed, older people typically overestimate

cues.zh: 而年轻人估得相当准。
cues.en: while younger people measure it quite accurately.

cues.zh: “好了，差不多停？”
cues.en: "Alright, probably stop?"
"Yep."

cues.zh: 哇，一分零二秒。
cues.en: Wooo, one minute, two seconds.

cues.zh: 一分零二秒。
cues.en: A minute and two seconds.

cues.zh: 一分零五秒。
cues.en: A minute and five.

cues.zh: 随着年龄增长，我们神经元的放电速率，也就是神经传导速度，会下降。
cues.en: As we get older, the rate at which our neurons fire, or our neuron conduction velocity, it decreases.

cues.zh: 你可以把这个放电速率想象成一块内部时钟。
cues.en: And you can think of this firing rate a little bit like an internal clock.

cues.zh: 所以，如果我们的内部时钟变慢了，就会让其他一切，也就是外部时间，
cues.en: And so, if our internal clock is slowing down, that would make everything else, external time,

cues.zh: 显得在加速。
cues.en: seem to be speeding up.

cues.zh: “我来告诉你时间。”
cues.en: "I'm going to tell you the time."

cues.zh: 现在？
cues.en: Now?

cues.zh: “现在。”
cues.en: "Now."

cues.zh: “一分钟。”
cues.en: "One minute."

cues.zh: 就这？刚才那是一分钟？
cues.en: That's it? That was one minute?

cues.zh: “一分钟。”
cues.en: "One minute."

cues.zh: 一分十七秒。
cues.en: Minute, seventeen seconds.

cues.zh: “还不错，对吧？”
cues.en: "Not bad, right?"

cues.zh: 不错。
cues.en: Not bad.

cues.zh: “我本以为会差得更多，不过看来并没有。”
cues.en: "I thought I'd be a lot closer actually, but I guess I wasn't."

cues.zh: 想知道实际是多久吗？
cues.en: Do you want to know what it really was?

cues.zh: 一分四十七秒。
cues.en: One minute forty seven.

cues.zh: “不可能，快两分钟了？居然真的快两分钟了。”
cues.en: "No way, it was almost two minutes? It was actually almost two minutes."

cues.zh: “时间过得真快，真是不可思议。”
cues.en: "It really is amazing how fast time flies by, it really is."

cues.zh: 我们对时间的感知，或者说时间知觉，并不像标准的五种感官之一。它没有专门的
cues.en: Our sense of time, or chronoception, is not like one of the standard five senses. It has no specialized

cues.zh: 感受器细胞，似乎也不局限于大脑的某一个区域。
cues.en: receptor cells and it does not appear to be localized in just one part of the brain.

cues.zh: 也许这说明它根本就不是一个统一的东西。
cues.en: Perhaps this suggests that it's not one coherent thing at all.

cues.zh: 但我们对时间的感知似乎非常基础。
cues.en: But it does seem that our perception of time is very fundamental.

cues.zh: 对老鼠的研究表明，即使切除它们的新皮层——也就是大脑中负责高级思维的
cues.en: Studies of rats have shown that even with their neocortex removed - that is, the higher order thinking

cues.zh: 部分——它们仍然能准确地学会计时四十秒。
cues.en: part of their brains- They are still able to learn how to time forty seconds accurately.

cues.zh: 这相当了不起，说明我们的时间感很早就进化出来了，是大脑的基本
cues.en: That's quite remarkable, and it suggests our sense of time evolved early and is one of the fundamental

cues.zh: 功能之一。
cues.en: functions of the brain.

cues.zh: 但这并不意味着我们的大脑总能忠实地表征时间。
cues.en: But that doesn't mean out brains always represent time faithfully.

cues.zh: 比如，你有没有注意到，特别好看的电影似乎比实际时长过得快得多？
cues.en: For example, have you noticed that really good movies seem to go by much faster than they actually are?

cues.zh: 或者你注意到假期飞逝而过？这都有充分的理由。
cues.en: Or do you notice that your vacations fly by? There are good reasons for this.

cues.zh: 当我们专注于某件事时，我们不会注意到时间在流逝，这让那些时刻感觉
cues.en: When we're focused on something, we don't notice that time is passing and that makes them feel in the moment

cues.zh: 比实际更短。
cues.en: shorter than they actually are.

cues.zh: 最好的情况下，这会产生一种叫“心流”的心理状态。这可以发生在打球或玩电子游戏时，
cues.en: At its best, this results in a mental state called "flow". This can happen when playing sports or video games

cues.zh: 或艺术家完全沉浸于工作时，或人们冥想时。
cues.en: or artists when they're fully engrossed in their work or people meditating.

cues.zh: 所以我认为，随着年龄增长时间加速的另一个原因，是我们更经常地沉浸于
cues.en: So I would argue another reason time speeds up as we age is because we are more often engrossed in

cues.zh: 正在做的事情中。
cues.en: what we're doing.

cues.zh: 还有一点似乎会让时间加速，那就是重复。我给大家看一组图片
cues.en: Another thing that appears to make time speed up is repetition. I'm going to show you a series of images

cues.zh: 请你们想一想，每张图片在屏幕上停留了多久。
cues.en: and I want you to consider how long each one appears on the screen.

cues.zh: 准备好了吗？
cues.en: Are you ready?

cues.zh: 开始。
cues.en: Go.

cues.zh: 哪一张看起来停留得最久？如果你和大多数人一样，大概会说是那只狗。
cues.en: So which one appeared to last the longest? If you're like most people, you'd probably say the dog.

cues.zh: 但其实那些图片在屏幕上停留的时间完全一样。狗之所以显得更久，
cues.en: But all of those images actually appeared on screen fore the same length of time. The dog seemed longer

cues.zh: 是因为它很新奇，因此你的大脑需要投入更多能量去处理它。
cues.en: because it was novel and therefore, your brain had to invest more energy in processing it.

cues.zh: 值得注意的是，我们对某件事持续多久的感觉——也就是主观时长——
cues.en: What's remarkable is that our sense of how long something is - or subjective duration-

cues.zh: 它与大脑消耗的能量高度相关。如果你研究人们一生中
cues.en: It correlates highly with how much energy we're using in our brains. Now, if you study how much energy people

cues.zh: 大脑消耗的能量，会发现大约在五岁时达到峰值。
cues.en: use in their brains over the course of their lifetime, you'll find that it peaks around age five.

cues.zh: 仔细想想，这其实挺合理，因为小时候几乎所有事物对你来说都是新鲜的。
cues.en: If you think about it, this kind of makes sense because when you're a kid, almost everything is novel to you.

cues.zh: 因此，你的大脑需要消耗更多能量，足足占你静息能量摄入的66%。
cues.en: And therefore, your brain needs to use more energy, fully 66% of your resting energy intake.

cues.zh: 大脑消耗这些能量是因为所有那些新奇的体验，而这至少在一定程度上
cues.en: That's used by the brain because of all the novel experiences and that must, at least in part,

cues.zh: 解释了为什么时间似乎过得更慢。
cues.en: explain why time appears to go more slowly.

cues.zh: 那么，我们能做些什么来让时间慢下来呢？研究表明，恐惧会增加我们对
cues.en: So, what can we do to slow time down? Well, studies have shown that being afraid increases our perception

cues.zh: 时间的感知。
cues.en: of time.

cues.zh: 当蜘蛛恐惧症患者被迫盯着蜘蛛看45秒时——是的，这真是个实验——
cues.en: When arachnophobes were forced to stare at spiders for 45 seconds - Yes, this is a real experiment -

cues.zh: 那些蜘蛛恐惧症患者认为那段经历持续的时间远超过45秒，
cues.en: Those arachnophobes judged that experience as lasting much longer than 45 seconds,

cues.zh: 正如你所预料的那样。
cues.en: as you would kind of expect.

cues.zh: 此外，涉及跳伞者或坠落者的实验表明，他们判断自己的经历持续
cues.en: Plus, experiments involving skydivers or people falling showed that they judged their experience to last

cues.zh: 的时间远比实际要长。
cues.en: much longer than it actually is.

cues.zh: 时间似乎过得很慢的另一种情况，是你感到无聊的时候。
cues.en: Another time when time appears to pass slowly is when you're bored.

cues.zh: “你知道，当你等啊等的时候，满脑子想的都是这件事，所以时间好像拖得没完没了。”
cues.en: "You know, when you're waiting and waiting, that's all you think about, so it seems like time drags forever."

cues.zh: 因为能关注的东西太少，你会敏锐地意识到时间正在流逝，
cues.en: Since there is so little to focus on, you are acutely aware of just how much time is passing,

cues.zh: 于是这些无聊的时刻就拖得格外漫长。
cues.en: and so these boring moments drag on and on.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你真想让自己对时间的感觉变慢，可以吓唬自己，去玩极限运动，
cues.en: So, if you really want to slow down your experience of time, you could scare yourself, take up extreme sports,

cues.zh: 出点事故，再在这些经历之间穿插一些无聊的时段。
cues.en: get into accidents and intersperse all of that with periods of boredom.

cues.zh: 但这种观点忽略了一个重要事实：我们体验时间的方式并不是单一的。
cues.en: But this viewpoint ignores one important fact, which is that we don't experience time as just one thing.

cues.zh: 我们会感受时间正在流逝，也会在回忆时感受它曾经如何流逝。
cues.en: We think about time as it passe, but also as it has passed before, when we remember it.

cues.zh: 而这两种看待时间的方式并不一致。
cues.en: And those two ways of looking at time, they don't align.

cues.zh: 比如说假期，感觉过得特别快，但回想起来，
cues.en: So for example, holidays, they feel like they go by really fast, but when you think back upon them,

cues.zh: 又觉得持续了很久。
cues.en: they last a long time.

cues.zh: 这是因为你经历了很多新鲜事，大脑形成了很多记忆。
cues.en: That's because you had a lot of novel experiences and your brain formed a lot of memories.

cues.zh: 大脑根据形成的记忆数量来判断假期时长。
cues.en: And it judges the duration of that vacation by the number of memories that were formed.

cues.zh: 新鲜感带来大量记忆，于是感觉过了很久，但身处其中时，又觉得很快。
cues.en: All that novelty means lots of memories means it feels like it took a long time, but in the moment, it felt fast.

cues.zh: 这就是悖论，我们时间感知的巨大悖论。
cues.en: This is the paradox, the great paradox, of our perception of time.

cues.zh: 如果你想让时间慢下来，有很多东西可以让你去体验，从而拖慢时间，
cues.en: If you want time to go slowly, there are a lot of things you can expose yourself to that will slow time down,

cues.zh: 但它们未必令人愉快。
cues.en: but they won't necessarily be pleasant.

cues.zh: 所以也许最幸福、记忆最长久的人生，恰恰是时间飞逝的那种。
cues.en: So maybe the happiest life and the longest remembered life is one where time really seems to fly.

cues.zh: 就像爱因斯坦说的：“把手放在火炉上一分钟，感觉像一小时。
cues.en: It's like Einstein said, "Put your hand on a stove for a minute and it'll feel like an hour.

cues.zh: 但坐在漂亮姑娘旁边一小时，感觉却像一分钟。”
cues.en: But sit next to a pretty girl for an hour and it'll feel like a minute."

cues.zh: 那么，你希望自己的人生感觉像什么？
cues.en: So, what would you like your life to feel like?

cues.en: And if you want to introduce more novelty into your life, than you should check out their series, "Brain Games"

cues.en: all of your senses, including your sense of time, chronoception.

cues.en: Did that feel like that lasted long?
